boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Saint Joseph’s traditions, from the Hawk’s nonstop wings to Latin diplomas and the annual Mass of the Holy Spirit.

cards.title: The Hawk Flaps Through the Whole Game
cards.subtitle: Saint Joseph’s basketball tradition
cards.notes: At a basketball game, watch for the costumed Hawk’s signature wings: the university says the mascot flaps nonstop, including at halftime.
cards.short_summary: The Hawk’s continuous wing-flapping is the school’s defining courtside ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s says the Hawk flaps its wings nonstop, even during halftime, throughout every basketball game.
cards.source_title: Facts and Figures | Saint Joseph's University
cards.access_notes: Observe during a Saint Joseph’s basketball game; game admission policies vary.

cards.title: Figure Eights During Timeouts
cards.subtitle: Saint Joseph’s basketball tradition
cards.notes: During timeouts, look for the Hawk “flying” figure eights around the court—an athletics page documents this specific mascot routine.
cards.short_summary: Timeouts get a distinctive figure-eight lap from the Hawk.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s Athletics documents that the Hawk “flies” in figure eights around the court during timeouts.
cards.source_title: Saint Joseph's Traditions | Saint Joseph's University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Observe during a Saint Joseph’s basketball game; game admission policies vary.

cards.title: The Hawk Will Never Die
cards.subtitle: University battle cry
cards.notes: Listen for or join the university’s documented battle cry at an appropriate campus or athletics event; it is tied directly to the Hawk mascot.
cards.short_summary: A rallying cry built around a mascot that never stops moving.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s identifies “The Hawk Will Never Die” as the University battle cry represented by the mascot’s nonstop flapping.
cards.source_title: Facts and Figures | Saint Joseph's University
cards.access_notes: Use in the context of campus spirit or athletics events.

cards.entity_name: “Oh When the Hawks Go Flying In”
cards.title: “Oh When the Hawks Go Flying In”
cards.subtitle: Saint Joseph’s fight song
cards.notes: Learn the refrain before a game: Saint Joseph’s lists this fight song as sung to the tune of “When the Saints Go Marching In.”
cards.short_summary: A Hawk-themed fight song set to a familiar marching tune.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s Athletics lists “Oh When the Hawks Go Flying In” as a fight song sung to the tune of “When the Saints, Go Marching In.”
cards.source_title: Saint Joseph's Traditions | Saint Joseph's University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Suitable for campus and athletics spirit settings.

cards.title: “Mine Eyes” Keeps the Hawk Flying
cards.subtitle: Saint Joseph’s fight song
cards.notes: Recognize this second listed fight song by its “Battle Hymn of the Republic” tune and its repeated Hawk-centered chorus.
cards.short_summary: A battle-hymn-style song that turns the Hawk into the central character.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s Athletics lists “Mine Eyes” as a fight song sung to the tune of “Battle Hymn of the Republic.”
cards.source_title: Saint Joseph's Traditions | Saint Joseph's University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Suitable for campus and athletics spirit settings.

cards.title: Crimson and Gray Came From a Book
cards.subtitle: University colors tradition
cards.notes: Spot the crimson and gray across campus materials and athletic gear; the university preserves the seminarian-and-book origin as tradition.
cards.short_summary: The school colors trace to a pep-rally story about a seminarian’s book.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s says tradition holds that crimson and gray were adopted in the 1890s after a seminarian saw the colors on a book at a pep rally.
cards.source_title: Facts and Figures | Saint Joseph's University
cards.access_notes: Visible in official university and athletics settings.

cards.title: Why Everyone Calls It Hawk Hill
cards.subtitle: City Avenue campus moniker
cards.notes: When visiting the City Avenue campus, note the Hawk Hill name and Barbelin Hall connection; the hawk-origin account is explicitly oral tradition.
cards.short_summary: The campus nickname grew from reports of hawks circling above Barbelin.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s Athletics says oral tradition attributes the “Hawk Hill” moniker to hawks seen circling above Barbelin Hall.
cards.source_title: Saint Joseph's Traditions | Saint Joseph's University Athletics
cards.access_notes: A campus name and historical reference; no special participation required.

cards.title: A 1903 Seal With Jesuit Symbols
cards.subtitle: Saint Joseph’s University seal
cards.notes: Find the official seal in university materials and examine its references to Saint Ignatius, the Society of Jesus and Saint Joseph.
cards.short_summary: An early-20th-century emblem carries the university’s Jesuit and patron-saint symbolism.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s says its University crest, used in the official seal, was originally designed in 1903 and references Jesuit history and Saint Joseph.
cards.source_title: Facts and Figures | Saint Joseph's University
cards.access_notes: View through official university publications and materials.

cards.title: Graduates Receive Diplomas in Latin
cards.subtitle: Saint Joseph’s commencement tradition
cards.notes: At commencement, notice the degree certificate’s Latin text; Saint Joseph’s links the practice to its historical Jesuit course of study.
cards.short_summary: A classical-language diploma remains part of Saint Joseph’s graduation practice.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s states that it upholds the tradition of providing graduates their diploma in Latin and provides an English translation.
cards.source_title: College of Arts and Sciences Undergraduate Ceremony Details | Saint Joseph's University
cards.access_notes: Applies to Saint Joseph’s graduates at commencement.

cards.title: The Annual Mass of the Holy Spirit
cards.subtitle: Opening-of-year university liturgy
cards.notes: Watch the campus calendar for this opening-of-year gathering, when the Saint Joseph’s community invokes the gifts of the Holy Spirit.
cards.short_summary: An annual beginning-of-year liturgy anchors the campus calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s describes its Mass of the Holy Spirit as an annual tradition in which the entire community gathers to invoke the gifts of the Holy Spirit for the new school year.
cards.access_notes: Listed by Campus Ministry as an annual event; check the campus calendar for the current date and location.
